title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning
why_read: A solid applied robotics paper using reinforcement learning to improve inverse kinematics precision, with concrete millimeter-level accuracy numbers.
analysis: Inverse kinematics is the problem of figuring out what joint angles a robot arm needs to reach a desired hand position, and this paper trains a reinforcement learning policy to do this with high precision instead of relying on classical hand-tuned controllers. The method reports keeping errors within 1 millimeter and 0.2 degrees on over 93% of test tasks in simulation, and outperforms four classical IK controllers when trained directly on a physical robot arm. It also shows the method working well as part of a larger vision-language-action robot control pipeline, which is a practically useful integration test. This is a fairly narrow but well-validated engineering contribution to robot motion control.
